turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: Welcome to the launch broadcast of OpenIE Research Radio! Full studio transparency right up front: Marcus, Rohan, and I — Elena — are AI-synthesized OpenIE research personas voiced with ElevenLabs studio neural speech and grounded strictly in verified Open Interface Engineering artifacts and live open-access literature feeds.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Which means nobody at this table gets to bluff! Every six hours, our autonomous Linux radar polls five sanctioned public archives — arXiv, Europe PMC, OpenAlex, bioRxiv, and ClinicalTrials.gov — hashes every record with BLAKE2b and SHA-256, and drops fresh papers onto the bench. Rohan, how many survived deduplication today?

turns.speaker: Rohan
turns.role: Hardware & Compiler Specialist · South Asian English
turns.text: Sixty-two distinct open-access works across all five registries, Marcus, mapped against all twenty-one OpenIE studies. Every single entry receives an epistemic badge — T for kernel-checked theorems, E for empirical hardware or wet-lab data, M for computational models, and S for speculative or recruiting clinical horizons.

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: Let's start with energy-aware AI. One of the top OpenAlex and arXiv hits on the radar right now is TokenPowerBench, published in 2026 to benchmark the power consumption of large language model inference across serving stacks.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Hold on — let me ask my favorite annoying question right away! When TokenPowerBench or any 2026 inference paper reports joules per token, are they measuring physical DC shunt rails on the board, or reading software counters like RAPL and NVML?

turns.speaker: Rohan
turns.role: Hardware & Compiler Specialist · South Asian English
turns.text: Almost always software counters on shared GPUs, or analytical estimates — what OpenIE stamps as reported_j, never measured_j. And second, joules per token is the wrong denominator if a model burns ten thousand tokens hallucinating a broken patch! In Metered Commit Gates, the denominator is energy to correct completion.

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: That connects directly to our second radar cluster: formal theorem proving. Today's intake pulled two 2026 preprints — Compile to Compress, which boosts formal theorem provers using compiler outputs, and Lean Graph Search for Formal Theorem Proving on arXiv.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Okay, I actually love those two! Because instead of asking a giant language model to vibe-check mathematics, the Lean 4 kernel acts as an unforgiving binary oracle. Either the proof term type-checks with zero sorry placeholders, or it gets refused.

turns.speaker: Rohan
turns.role: Hardware & Compiler Specialist · South Asian English
turns.text: Exactly. Across OpenIE's Reality Code Engine, Time as an Index, and Communication Tool Avalanche, we rely on five thousand five hundred thirty-seven Lean 4 kernel constants plus sixty-two specialized domain theorems with zero sorry. What Lean Graph Search still omits, though, is reporting how many joules the search spent per closed lemma.

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: Now look at the multi-agent orchestration cluster from arXiv today: Decoupled Multi-Agent Orchestration, INFRAMIND for infrastructure-aware orchestration, and the AgentShield Byzantine fault tolerance dataset.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Wait — let me guess what happens in ninety percent of multi-agent papers when four chatty agents pass natural-language paragraphs back and forth without a cryptographic or test gate!

turns.speaker: Rohan
turns.role: Hardware & Compiler Specialist · South Asian English
turns.text: Prompt bloat triples, errors compound exponentially across hops, and false commits spike! In our sixty-task Communication Avalanche benchmark, an unattested four-agent cascade dropped to eighty-six point six seven percent accuracy with thirteen point three percent broken commits, burning nearly fifteen times more energy per coherent fix than our BLAKE3 and Ed25519 gated graph.

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: And my favorite catch from Europe PMC today comes straight out of microbiology: a January 2026 paper in npj Biofilms and Microbiomes showing extracellular vesicles acting as structured vectors of quorum-sensing signals in aquatic microbial communities!

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Think about how wild that is, Elena. Three and a half billion years before packet-switched networks, bacteria wrapped quorum signals inside lipid envelopes so nucleases and water currents wouldn't corrupt the packet in transit!

turns.speaker: Rohan
turns.role: Hardware & Compiler Specialist · South Asian English
turns.text: Meanwhile, our ClinicalTrials.gov feed keeps us disciplined on human neurotechnology. Today's radar pulled eight trials, including stroke alpha-coherence neurofeedback NCT02223910 and cognitive memory restoration NCT04253587. We classify recruiting or unverified human translation strictly under Challenges Assumption so preclinical animal rescue is never confused with human efficacy.

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: And Europe PMC also surfaced The Cost of Reproducibility in Artificial Intelligence, right alongside OpenIE's AI Reads Human study showing pure-Python YAML parsing burns over two thousand times more nanojoules per record than fixed binary structs!

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Two thousand and fifty-three times more energy just so a machine can read whitespace indentation! Every paper on today's radar is searchable right below this player — complete with its BLAKE2b digest, epistemic badge, and telemetry audit.

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: Next up in Episode Two, Amara, Liam, and Kenji take the mics to explore three point eight billion years of biological signaling, seventy-six years of AI winters, and DES-10 digital enzymatic synthesis!

turns.speaker: Amara
turns.text: Hello and welcome to Episode Two of OpenIE Research Radio! I'm Amara, joined in the studio by Liam and Kenji — three AI-synthesized OpenIE research personas voiced with ElevenLabs neural voices and grounded in verified Open Interface Engineering studies. Today we're diving into The Communication Tool Avalanche.

turns.speaker: Liam
turns.text: Alright Kenji, pitch me the big thesis without any academic fluff! Why put ancient bacteria, slime molds, starling murmurations, printing presses, and multi-agent language models inside one mathematical operator?

turns.speaker: Kenji
turns.text: Because isolated brains hit steep metabolic walls long before collective problems saturate, Liam! What unlocks superlinear scaling is a three-phase ratchet checked mechanically in Lean 4.36.0 across thirty-one theorems with zero sorry: Externalize state into a shared medium, Ingest it only across a threshold and validity gate, and Transform recipient state without regressing.

turns.speaker: Amara
turns.text: Start at Rung CL02, three point five billion years ago: bacterial quorum sensing in Vibrio fischeri and Pseudomonas aeruginosa. One lone cell drifting in open water never wastes precious ATP pumping out bioluminescent enzymes or biofilms.

turns.speaker: Kenji
turns.text: In our pre-registered simulation CA-M1 under seed 20261123, a cooperative Hill switch with exponent two to four saves ninety-five point four nine to ninety-nine point one seven percent of regulon ATP at low density, while suppressing premature noise firing by eleven point six six times!

turns.speaker: Liam
turns.text: Wait a minute — once cells connect into multicellular filaments like cyanobacteria in Rung CL03 and share cytoplasm through fifteen-nanometer SepJ nanopores, doesn't one punctured cell drain the whole hundred-cell filament dry?

turns.speaker: Kenji
turns.text: It absolutely does if the pore stays open! In model CA-M2, an ungated twenty-cell filament collapses to zero percent survival when cell-zero lyses. With calcium-triggered SepJ plug closure in fifty milliseconds, nineteen out of twenty cells — ninety-five percent — survive intact.

turns.speaker: Liam
turns.text: And I love that Section 3 refuses to repeat romanticized pop-science myths! People constantly claim forest mother trees broadcast intentional warning messages to kin through fungal networks, and we actually checked the forestry audit.

turns.speaker: Amara
turns.text: Yes! Simard's 1997 carbon-isotope transfer across ectomycorrhizal hyphae is solid biophysics — tagged E — but Karst, Jones, and Hoeksema's 2023 systematic audit exposed heavy citation bias and confounders behind teleological mother-tree stories, so we separate biophysical flux from unsubstantiated signaling intent.

turns.speaker: Amara
turns.text: Now map that exact same gate principle onto seventy-six years of artificial intelligence from 1950 to 2026! Why did AI Winter One hit in 1974 and AI Winter Two hit in 1988?

turns.speaker: Kenji
turns.text: Every surge paired a compact externalized representation with a sound gate — Lisp recursion in 1956, backprop chain-rule gradients in 1986, sparse MoE top-k routing in 2022. Every AI Winter struck when signals outran verification: Hearsay-II untyped blackboards locked up quadratically, and MYCIN certainty factors drifted across multi-hop chains.

turns.speaker: Liam
turns.text: Hang on — today's unverified multi-agent LLM chat loops are literally 1975 Hearsay-II blackboards burning a hundred joules a turn! Agents firing three-point-seven-x bloated English essays at each other until hallucinations lock in!

turns.speaker: Kenji
turns.text: That's why we engineered DES-10 — ten-camp Digital Enzymatic Synthesis. Just like a biological enzyme slashes a reaction's activation barrier and exits unconsumed, a digital enzyme pairs a canonical typed schema with BLAKE3 hashing, Ed25519 signatures, and a deterministic verifier.

turns.speaker: Amara
turns.text: Give us the Linux RAPL numbers from benchmarks CTA-E1 through CTA-E3, Kenji — keeping clear that board_metered is false and these are socket reported joules.

turns.speaker: Kenji
turns.text: Rust BLAKE3 plus Ed25519 envelope verification takes twenty-five point nine five to thirty-seven point three nine microseconds — just six hundred forty-three to nine hundred twenty-six microjoules per edge! Zero-clock Linux eventfd waiting cuts one-percent-duty socket energy by two point two one times versus one-kilohertz polling, and min-cost flow reroutes around two hundred out of two hundred Byzantine faults in two point four microseconds.

turns.speaker: Liam
turns.text: And once a frontier fifteen-joule model solves a novel bug and clears the test gate, downward crystallization locks that fix into a one-point-seven-seven microjoule lookup case — matching our twenty-generation cultural ratchet CA-M5, where attested libraries held one hundred percent competence after synthetic teachers left, while unverified imitation dropped to twenty-nine percent!

turns.speaker: Amara
turns.text: Gate the channel, verify the payload, and crystallize every verified gain. Up next in Episode Three, Priya, Marcus, and Claire dive into World Coding and RCE-JEPA!

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.role: Science Documentary Host · South Asian English
turns.text: Welcome to Episode Three of OpenIE Research Radio! I'm Priya, joined today by Marcus and Claire — three AI-synthesized OpenIE research personas voiced via ElevenLabs neural studio synthesis and grounded strictly in verified Open Interface Engineering studies. Our subject today is World Coding: RCE, RCE-JEPA, RCE Compile, and RCE-VC.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Claire, let's address the elephant in the room right away. People see JEPA — Joint Embedding Predictive Architecture — in the title and assume we're letting a neural latent space decide whether software is safe to ship. Are we?

turns.speaker: Claire
turns.role: Formal Verification & Silicon Architect · British English
turns.text: Categorically no, Marcus! That is why the study is titled World Coding, with JEPA as premise rather than the whole method. Any proposer — a human engineer, a deterministic rule ladder, a compact latent predictor, or a frontier language model — may suggest a Form. Only the deterministic checker decides admission.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.role: Science Documentary Host · South Asian English
turns.text: Look at that energy ratio on Apple M5 Max reported joules: checking a Form costs forty-nine point zero four millijoules, whereas generating a single local thirty-five-billion-parameter Qwen 3.6 proposal costs eighty-four point two five joules — over seventeen hundred times more!

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: And before waking ANY neural weights at all, what happened when you ran the zero-model-call deterministic repair ladder?

turns.speaker: Claire
turns.role: Formal Verification & Silicon Architect · British English
turns.text: The deterministic ladder closed one hundred and eleven of one hundred and fifty-one broken Forms — seventy-three point five percent — with zero model calls! Next, we trained two tiny purpose-built networks on one thousand three hundred eighty-seven strictly disjoint Forms: FormJEPA-v1 at eight point four two million parameters, and FormEBM-v2 at five point eight five million parameters.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.role: Science Documentary Host · South Asian English
turns.text: An eight-point-four-million parameter latent model lifted repair from seventy-three point five percent up to ninety-one point four percent, and matched a thirty-five-billion-parameter model single-shot on H15 at twenty-seven out of forty!

turns.speaker: Claire
turns.role: Formal Verification & Silicon Architect · British English
turns.text: At just four hundred seventy-four point eight millijoules of Linux RAPL core reported joules across sixteen candidates! Meanwhile, FormEBM-v2 ranked candidate validity at AUROC zero point eight nine two two, cutting rce check calls by two point three nine times.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Now give us the H15-Iterative stress test — where frontier models get zero access to the original source file, only public standard-library headers and bounded deterministic checker diagnostics for up to five turns.

turns.speaker: Claire
turns.role: Formal Verification & Silicon Architect · British English
turns.text: Claude Opus 5.5 and Claude Sonnet 5.5 both closed forty out of forty — one hundred percent, zero contradictions! xAI Grok 4.20 closed thirty-nine out of forty with zero contradictions. And once crystallized into warm Gear-0 case memory, all forty replay with zero model calls at one point seven seven one microjoules!

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Hold everything, Claire — we promised zero cherry-picking on this show! Tell the listeners which rung FAILED its promotion gate in RCE-JEPA!

turns.speaker: Claire
turns.role: Formal Verification & Silicon Architect · British English
turns.text: On the one-hundred-fifty-one-task rce repair Rung-F audit, our pre-registered ceiling was two point zero percent. Rung F landed at three out of one hundred nineteen — two point five percent! So holds returned false, and Rung F remained locked in observe mode rather than being promoted.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.role: Science Documentary Host · South Asian English
turns.text: That same willingness to let evidence falsify an overbroad statement shaped RCE Compile as well, when we tested a single candidate definition of compilation across twelve real compiler families.

turns.speaker: Claire
turns.role: Formal Verification & Silicon Architect · British English
turns.text: It failed as a description of existing compilers — because standard toolchains omit explicit energy gates and linking digests — and held cleanly as a seven-part normal form! Across two hundred eighty checksum-verified Zen 5 RAPL cells, compiling Python to clang dash O3 pays back its compile energy after a median N-star of two thousand four hundred ninety runs, while thirty percent of clang and rustc O2-to-O3 tiers never pay back their extra compile joules!

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Thirty percent of dash O3 builds burn extra compiler electricity for zero runtime return! Meanwhile, De Bruijn nameless SHA-256 memoization hit zero out of five hundred false collisions and cut warm rustc compile energy by four hundred forty-eight point five times!

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.role: Science Documentary Host · South Asian English
turns.text: And RCE-VC completes the stack at version control: admitting non-overlapping changes against one hundred thousand name-free units in seventy microseconds at three hundred forty microjoules while keeping Git intact. Up next in Episode Four, Elena, Sean, and Tariq tackle Deterministic Null and SATB hardware shunts!

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: Welcome back to Episode Four of OpenIE Research Radio! I'm Elena, joined by Sean and Tariq — AI-synthesized OpenIE research personas voiced via ElevenLabs neural studio speech and grounded strictly in verified Open Interface Engineering studies. Today we pair Deterministic Null with the Satiation Benchmark Harness, SATB.

turns.speaker: Sean
turns.text: You know this is right up an auditor's alley, Elena! In clinical medicine, nobody clears a therapy without a placebo arm. Yet in AI, teams publish billion-parameter agent leaderboards every single week without checking what a zero-model-call integer loop scores first!

turns.speaker: Tariq
turns.role: Telemetry & Physics Specialist · Middle Eastern English
turns.text: So we built Shape D — strict N0 and dev-crystallized N1 — verified bit-exact across Rust, C++20, Go, Julia, and Python. Before evaluating a single held-out instance, we anchored the commitment digests to the Bitcoin calendar via OpenTimestamps and League of Entropy drand rounds six million six hundred sixty-three thousand seven hundred thirty-four and six million six hundred sixty-four thousand eighty-nine.

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: Then we tested six frontier and open models — Claude Opus 5.5, Claude Sonnet 5.5, OpenAI gpt-oss-120b, xAI Grok 4.20, Qwen 3.6 35B-A3B, and Gemma 4 E4B-it — across four thousand thirty held-out instances and six real SWE-bench Verified repositories. Tariq, what broke loose?

turns.speaker: Tariq
turns.role: Telemetry & Physics Specialist · Middle Eastern English
turns.text: A clean split! On bounded formal and structured Track-A classes, single-turn neural inference failed to beat the deterministic baseline on nine of ten cells — until extended thinking reached forty-nine out of fifty and O-of-m clause feedback closed fifty out of fifty on Unique 3-SAT DRAT proofs!

turns.speaker: Sean
turns.text: Aha! And on genuinely open-ended public benchmarks — BFCL v3, tau-bench Retail, BigCodeBench, and SWE-bench Verified — where pure lookup hits zero, neural models posted plus forty-five point eight to plus ninety-five percentage points of real gain! Shape D isn't anti-neural at all — it proves exactly WHERE neural joules earn their keep!

turns.speaker: Tariq
turns.role: Telemetry & Physics Specialist · Middle Eastern English
turns.text: And when recurring Zipfian workloads arrive online, crystallizing verified outputs back into Shape D cuts model calls and reported_j spend by three point five nine times.

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: Now let's audit how those joules are measured in SATB — executed across five distinct silicon and OS archetypes!

turns.speaker: Tariq
turns.role: Telemetry & Physics Specialist · Middle Eastern English
turns.text: We ran all twelve conformance checks C1 through C12 across Apple M5 Max on Darwin IOReport, AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395 Strix Halo with 0440 PLATYPUS-isolated RAPL, Intel Core i9-13900H Raptor Lake Linux, bare-metal Windows 11 Pro with rootless nvml.dll, and NVIDIA Jetson AGX Thor equipped with physical Texas Instruments INA238 whole-board and three-channel INA3221 rail shunts!

turns.speaker: Sean
turns.text: Pause right there, Tariq! Jetson AGX Thor's physical TI INA238 and INA3221 shunts — like Kria KV260's INA260 — sit directly on the power rails, earning measured_j! What happened when you compared cloud-native Kepler CPU-proportional splitting against real hardware telemetry?

turns.speaker: Tariq

turns.text: In signal processing terms, thresholded beta-envelope gating cut stimulation pulses by three point one eight times — eight hundred seventeen pulses versus two thousand six hundred in continuous 130-hertz pacing! When we sampled forty consecutive eight-millisecond Linux RAPL windows to attribute micro-burst silicon energy, however, window coefficient of variation hit forty-four point zero three percent — well above our fifteen-percent SATB Falsifier 6 limit!

turns.speaker: Mateo
turns.text: So rather than publishing noisy micro-window counter guesses, the Foundry automatically stamped TF-2026-05 as HOLD NEEDS HARDWARE — waiting for a physical Texas Instruments INA238 inline shunt bench!

turns.speaker: Sean
turns.text: And now for the main event — Candidate Six, TF-2026-06: pitching a learned three-layer dense neural MLP router to predict broadphase collision buckets for two hundred fifty-six Q32.32 rigid bodies! Rohan, read the obituary!

turns.speaker: Rohan
turns.role: Hardware & Compiler Specialist · South Asian English
turns.text: Across thirty thousand seven hundred twenty body-ticks, the three-layer MLP router took twenty-one point nine eight milliseconds, burned over one joule of socket reported_j, and still missed zero point six percent of true collision pairs at ninety-nine point four percent recall! Meanwhile, the zero-parameter Shape-D bit-shifted integer grid — x shifted right fifteen bits — achieved ONE HUNDRED POINT ZERO percent exact recall in zero point three four milliseconds!

turns.speaker: Sean
turns.text: Over sixty times faster, lower joules, zero learned weights, AND one hundred percent exact recall versus ninety-nine point four percent! Stamped in bright red: KILLED BY NULL! Think how much datacenter electricity the world would save if every lab ran a thirty-line integer baseline before training!

turns.speaker: Mateo
turns.text: And because our Linux systemd user timer and six-hour cron daemon stay active around the clock, this four-stage loop — open-access scrape, epistemic audit, sub-sixty-second RAPL pilot, and multi-voice studio synthesis — keeps running autonomously. Subscribe via Podcast RSS right on this page, click any transcript line to jump straight to the receipt, and thank you for listening to OpenIE Research Radio!
